Reference / os/process

os/process#

Process owns one shared lazy runtime state.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let process = Process(command: command);
let input = ProcessInput(origin: process);
input.write(payload);
input.close();
let exit = await process.exit();

Description#

Process owns one shared lazy runtime state. Constructing Process and its stream views does not spawn. id(), running(), exit(), signal() and every stream operation start the command exactly once. close() is the exception: closing an unstarted Process never launches it.

Close stdin to deliver EOF without terminating the child:

Direct users must drain stdout and stderr concurrently with waiting when a child can produce substantial output. CommandCapture provides that higher- level orchestration. Process.close() is idempotent; it forcefully stops and reaps a running child and discards unread pipe data.

Process.errors#

Its standard error, read blocking.

Process.streams#

streams() is ProcessStreams

The child's standard streams, asynchronous (#196): reading its output or writing its input waits without holding up other tasks.

let child = Process(command);
await child.streams().input().write("query\n");
for await child.streams().output().lines() -> line {
    …
}

They sit next to input(), output() and errors(), which block. A stream read asynchronously once is read so afterwards. streams() starts the process.
